To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gold nanoparticles can be toxic to zebrafish embryos, but that the toxicity is dependent on the size, shape, surface charge and coating of the nanoparticles.
GNSs were less toxic to zebrafish embryos than GNRs, and that GNR toxicity was significantly reduced by coating the nanorods with a double layer of PSS and PAH.
the toxicity of gold nanorods is ameliorated by surface coating with polystyrenesulphate and, to a greater extent, with both polystyrensulphate and polyallamine.

the surface properties of gold nanorods are a major determinant of their toxicity.
